beginner.headline: Nigella Lawson Joins Bake Off as New Judge
beginner.brief: Nigella Lawson is a new judge on The Great British Bake Off. Many critics praised her new role. The show returns to TV later this month. She is taking over from Dame Prue Leith. New contestants are confirmed for the 17th series. A doctor and a hairdresser are among the contestants.

intermediate.headline: Nigella Lawson Joins Bake Off’s New Series
intermediate.brief: TV critics have welcomed Nigella Lawson as a new judge on The Great British Bake Off. Channel 4 will show the first episode of series 17 on 22 September. The opening episode was shown to critics earlier this week. Lawson replaces Prue Leith, who wanted to spend less time working and more time enjoying herself. Anita Singh of the Telegraph suggested that Lawson’s memorable comments could become popular on social media. The new participants have different backgrounds, including work in medicine, hairdressing and the arts. Moyin is a student who balances his studies with athletics. He uses flavours inspired by his Nigerian heritage in his baking. Yannis is a doctor who wants to challenge an unfair belief about Bangladeshi men cooking. Connie works in a hospital and uses baking to relax after a busy day.

advanced.headline: Critics Welcome Nigella Lawson to Bake Off
advanced.brief: Early reviews have lauded Nigella Lawson’s arrival as a judge on The Great British Bake Off. The seventeenth series premieres on Channel 4 on 22 September, following a preview for television reviewers. Lawson succeeds Prue Leith, who said she wanted to reduce her workload and enjoy more free time. Ben Dowell of the Times portrayed the production team as delighted by Lawson’s presence. His comparison with royalty conveys admiration rather than a claim about her actual status. The Telegraph’s Anita Singh depicted Lawson as a source of material likely to circulate on social media. Her metaphor, “a walking meme factory,” emphasizes the potential for Lawson’s comments to become widely shared online jokes. The announced roster brings together a doctor, a sprinter, a hairdresser and a drag artist. Drawing on his Nigerian roots, Moyin incorporates distinctive flavours into his bakes while combining university studies with athletics. Yannis, a doctor, hopes to counter the stereotype that Bangladeshi men do not belong in the kitchen. Connie, who works in hospital discharge services, describes baking as a way to unwind after a demanding day. These accounts describe the bakers’ interests and aspirations; they do not establish how well each person will perform in the competition.
